Definition: of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian:--Quartus.
BiblicalUsage: Quartus appears once, in the greetings at the end of Romans, where Paul calls him simply "a brother" alongside Gaius and Erastus in Romans 16:23. He is not given a title or a task in the letter, only a place among the saints who send their greeting.
TheologicalSignificance: For me, Quartus matters because the gospel made room for ordinary brothers whose names we would never know if Paul had not written them down.
